title: Indication Subsystem — sound + visual + macOS notification cues
notes: Implement an indication facade so the user always knows what the daemon is doing. Three backends (SoundBackend via injected SoundCueProcessor with IndicationCueFrame brackets; VisualBackend via JSONL tailed by watch.py; NotificationBackend via osascript with argv-only construction). Mode-aware gating, per-kind toggles, cooldown, quiet hours. Wires ~30 events across T1/T2/T3.

stories.title: NotificationBackend (macOS osascript, argv-only, injection-safe)
stories.description: Implement src/indication_backends/notification.py. Body/title pass via subprocess argv ('on run argv' AppleScript reads via 'item N of argv'). Never interpolates user text into AppleScript source. Darwin guard at construction. 2s subprocess timeout.
acceptanceCriteria: src/indication_backends/notification.py exists; on non-Darwin (sys.platform != 'darwin') backend disables itself at construction (fire becomes no-op)
fire() builds: cmd = ['osascript', '-e', 'on run argv', '-e', '<display notification line>', '-e', 'end run', '--', body, title, *(sound_name if non-empty)]
Body and title are NEVER concatenated into the AppleScript source string
When level→sound_name is empty (info/success/long_running): AppleScript omits 'sound name (item 3 of argv)' clause; argv length == 2 (body, title)
When level→sound_name is non-empty (attention/error/input_waiting): AppleScript includes the 'sound name (item 3 of argv)' clause; argv length == 3 (body, title, sound_name)
Subprocess uses asyncio.create_subprocess_exec with stdout=DEVNULL, stderr=PIPE; timeout=2.0 wraps proc.wait(); on timeout proc.kill() is called
tests/test_indication_notification.py mocks asyncio.create_subprocess_exec, parametrizes both arities (sound vs no-sound), asserts rendered script lines and argv length per case

Injection regression test: pass body containing '"; do shell script "echo PWNED"; display notification "' — asserts (a) returncode 0 from mocked osascript, (b) the literal payload string is delivered as an argv item (captured by mock), (c) NO PWNED side-effect anywhere (no echo into stdout/stderr/files), (d) no exception raised
Non-Darwin skip test: monkeypatch sys.platform to 'linux'; assert NotificationBackend disables and fire is a no-op

stories.title: Runtime disable / re-enable (Indication.reload)
stories.description: Implement Indication.reload(settings). Lock-and-flag-flip-before-drain ordering: acquire lock, set _enabled=False, release lock, drain pending dispatch tasks (with timeout), aclose backends, optionally re-init if newly enabled. Add a thin file-watcher or signal-handler hook in main.py that triggers reload when ~/.heare/config.toml [indication].enabled flips.
acceptanceCriteria: Indication.reload(settings) follows the documented sequence: (1) acquire lock + self._enabled=False; (2) release lock; (3) drain pending dispatch tasks with bounded timeout; (4) aclose() on each backend (per-backend try/except); (5) re-read settings; if enabled, re-init backends and set _enabled=True
Any notify() arriving between steps 1 and 5 sees _enabled=False under the lock and short-circuits; never enqueues into a closing backend

tests/test_indication_runtime_disable.py: start enabled=True, fire a cue (recorded), call reload(disabled), fire another (NOT recorded), call reload(enabled), fire (recorded). Assert backends close cleanly between transitions; no daemon restart
main.py wires either a SIGHUP handler or a config file mtime watcher that triggers reload on change (one-line hook is acceptable)
